learningObjectives: Use hardware button and orientation Modules to simulate physical device interaction.
Distinguish Android emulator/iOS simulator biometric Modules from provider-specific cloud examples.
Move files on and off the device and manage Appium session lifecycle explicitly.
Apply a systematic troubleshooting checklist to mobile automation failures.

elements.title: Simulating physical device controls
items: ME3.0 Hardware Button Operations — supports Home on Android/iOS and Back/ApplicationSelector on Android. Its documented values do not include volume or power.
ME3.0 Set Device Orientation — rotates the device between portrait and landscape, for apps or screens whose layout or behaviour changes with orientation.

bulletPoints: Use the documented platform-specific Home, Back and ApplicationSelector operations.
Set Device Orientation = rotate portrait/landscape for orientation-dependent flows.

elements.title: Biometric automation Modules
items: Use Android fingerprint authentication — supplies a configured fingerprint ID on an Android emulator, not a universal physical-device fingerprint override.
Use iOS biometric authentication — supplies positive/negative FaceID or TouchID results on an iOS simulator.
Set iOS biometrics enrollment — enables/disables simulator enrollment before simulated authentication.

Tosca Cloud documentation separately describes Perfecto biometrics and image-injection Modules. This does not establish their availability or setup in every on-prem Standard subset; confirm the installed product/version and provider configuration.

elements.text: Enrollment and authentication are separate simulator settings. Simulated results exercise application behavior without validating real biometric hardware.

bulletPoints: Use the correct emulator/simulator Module and prerequisite enrollment.
Simulated authentication is not physical sensor evidence.
Confirm provider-specific Module availability for the actual installed product.

elements.title: Moving data and managing sessions
items: Upload File to Mobile Device / Download File from Mobile Device — documented Android file transfer. Existing destination files can be overwritten; transferring a file does not verify its business contents.
Get Appium Session Id — retrieves the underlying session identifier, useful when correlating Tosca execution against raw Appium/TMA logs during troubleshooting.
End Appium Session — ends the current session. Device-farm reservation release remains provider-specific; do not equate session completion with guaranteed immediate availability.

bulletPoints: The documented file-transfer Modules target Android and may overwrite destinations.
Get Appium Session Id helps correlate Tosca-level failures with raw driver logs.
End the current session and separately verify provider reservation/release behavior.

elements.term: A dedicated Module for a transient component
elements.description: Android Snackbar offers Text and Action steering. Use appropriate synchronization such as WaitOn before verifying the message or choosing its action; the Module name does not guarantee correct timing or successful interaction.

bulletPoints: Synchronize with the Snackbar before verification or action.

elements.title: When a mobile TestCase fails to connect or execute
items: Confirm the intended prepared device is detected and available in the Agent.
Compare effective TCPs and application identifiers with the failed operation.
For remote use, verify the configured REST/Appium services and reachability from the execution machine.
Inspect driver/session logs and run a minimal opening test.
Investigate network, device, driver and app causes according to the evidence rather than a rigid universal order.

elements.title: Separate symptoms from confirmed causes
items: Session creation errors can have multiple causes; confirm the effective endpoint, target and logs.
OS/Finder visibility does not prove debugging authorization or Agent readiness.
For an APK certificate error, verify the supplied signature and request a compatible signed test build; do not infer v1-only signing or automatically replace the key.
A scan can succeed while execution differs in configuration, state or timing; compare those differences instead of inventing a parser defect.

bulletPoints: Discovery and session execution are separate checks.
Use the actual failing layer and logs to prioritize investigation.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Android and iOS biometric Modules are interchangeable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using the Android fingerprint Module against an iOS biometric prompt, or vice versa.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the platform-specific emulator/simulator Modules and their prerequisites. They do not provide a universal real-device biometric override.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to simulate iOS biometric authentication without setting enrollment first
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Calling the iOS biometric authentication Module against a simulator that has never been configured as having biometrics enrolled.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure iOS simulator enrollment before requesting a simulated authentication result; distinguish this from validating a physical sensor.

examPitfalls.title: Letting Appium sessions linger on a shared device
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Finishing a TestCase without explicitly ending its Appium session, leaving the device unavailable to the next test or teammate until a timeout expires.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: End the current Appium session and confirm provider-specific reservation/release behavior. Do not promise immediate availability across all device farms.

examPitfalls.title: Interpreting connection error text literally
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reading 'Ensure that the requested device is connected' and spending time reconnecting or replacing the device.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the actual device, effective configuration and session logs. The message alone does not prove a particular trailing-slash defect or rule out networking.

practiceQuiz.scenario: On an iOS simulator, what must be configured before Use iOS biometric authentication?

options.text: The device's region and language settings.
Biometrics enrollment must be set via Set iOS biometrics enrollment.
The app must be reinstalled immediately beforehand.
LiveView must be enabled.

practiceQuiz.hint: Enrollment and authentication are two separate steps on iOS.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Enable simulator biometrics enrollment before supplying an authentication result. This simulates the flow and does not validate physical biometric hardware.

optionExplanations.A: Region/language settings do not enable simulator enrollment.
optionExplanations.B: Configure simulator enrollment for the simulated authentication flow.
optionExplanations.C: Universal immediate reinstallation is not this prerequisite.
optionExplanations.D: Execution preview does not enroll biometrics.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A brief 'Item deleted — Undo' bar appears at the bottom of an Android screen and auto-dismisses after a few seconds. Which Module is purpose-built for steering it?

options.text: Click On Screen
Android Snackbar
ME3.0 Hardware Button Operations
Send Text Input To Focused Control

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a named Android UI component, not a generic gesture.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Android Snackbar provides Text and Action attributes for this component. Synchronize with its appearance before verification or action; the Module does not guarantee timing by itself.

optionExplanations.A: This is a position-based gesture rather than the component-specific Module.
optionExplanations.B: This is the documented component-specific Module.
optionExplanations.C: Hardware button operations do not steer this message component.
optionExplanations.D: Text input does not verify or act on the Snackbar.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Mobile Scan succeeds but TestCase session creation fails. Which evidence-driven investigation is appropriate?

options.text: Whether the device's USB cable is faulty.
Compare effective endpoint/device configuration and inspect the failed-session logs.
Whether the device needs a factory reset.
Whether the app under test has been updated.

practiceQuiz.hint: Successful scanning is useful evidence, not a complete root-cause diagnosis.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Scan and execution may differ in effective settings or state. Check configuration and logs without assuming a particular parsing defect or excluding network/device/driver failures.

optionExplanations.A: No evidence yet isolates a faulty cable.
optionExplanations.B: These checks examine the failed operation without guessing its cause.
optionExplanations.C: Erasing the device is not justified by this symptom.
optionExplanations.D: An update alone is not established as the cause.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does End Appium Session do after the last intended operation in the current session?

options.text: It improves control identification accuracy.
Ends the current Appium session; provider reservation release must be verified separately.
It is required before Upload File to Mobile Device can run.
It disables biometric prompts for the next session.

practiceQuiz.hint: Session lifecycle and cloud reservation lifecycle are not necessarily identical.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Module ends the current session. Immediate reuse of a cloud device depends on the provider’s reservation/release behavior rather than this Module alone.

optionExplanations.A: Ending a session does not change identification accuracy.
optionExplanations.B: This is the documented session action, with release checked separately.
optionExplanations.C: File transfer is not enabled by first ending its active session.
optionExplanations.D: The Module does not disable future biometric prompts.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A device is listed as Ready, but session creation fails. Which check complements discovery evidence?

options.text: Factory-reset the device before inspecting configuration
Check effective connection settings, execution-host reachability and session logs
Whether the app under test needs to be reinstalled.
The device's biometric enrollment status.

practiceQuiz.hint: A listed device does not prove that an automation session works.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use configuration, reachability and logs to diagnose the failed operation. Device discovery alone cannot rule out all other layers or justify reinstalling or erasing the app/device.

optionExplanations.A: Erasing the device before diagnosis is not supported by the evidence.
optionExplanations.B: These checks complement discovery with session-related evidence.
optionExplanations.C: Reinstallation is not justified from Ready status alone.
optionExplanations.D: Enrollment matters for biometric flows, not every session-creation failure.

quickRecap.value: Home on Android/iOS; Back and ApplicationSelector on Android. Orientation uses Portrait/Landscape.
Android emulator fingerprint and iOS simulator biometric Modules require their documented prerequisites.
Upload/Download target Android; inspect overwritten files and verify contents separately.
Capture the session ID for logs and end the current session; provider reservation release is separate.
Use Text/Action with synchronization before message verification or action.
Compare effective settings, execution-host reachability and failed-session logs.
Error wording alone is not a root-cause diagnosis.
